newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco court to examine Moslem militant sentences.
newsitem.headline: Morocco court to examine Moslem militant sentences.

text.p: Morocco's supreme court will examine on Tuesday the case of six Moslem militants, three under death sentences, who were convicted of an armed attack on a hotel in Marrakesh in which two Spaniards died in 1994, a lawyer said on Monday.
Two members of the group are French nationals of Algerian origin.

"The Rabat supreme court will examine on Tuesday the case of the six people and issue a final decision...But as usual none of the convicts would appear before the court," Moroccan barrister Abdessalam Chaouch told Reuters.
Hamel Marzouk, Redouane Hammadi and Stephane Ait Idir were sentenced to death by a court of appeal in the central city of Fez in January 1995.
Marzouk and Ait Idir are French nationals of Algerian origin. Moroccans Kamal Benakcha, Abdessalam Guerouaz and Abderrahman Boujedli were sentenced to life imprisonment.
The six were among 17 men and one woman, all of Moroccan or Algerian origin, arrested after the armed attack against the Atlas Asni luxury hotel in the tourist city of Marrakesh in August 1994.
The other defendants were sentenced to prison terms ranging from six months to 10 years.
